text: A phished service account signs into Oakmere's tenant from a country it has never touched -- and two separate exclusions, built for two separate reasons, both quietly let it through.
No alert fires. The first real signal comes a day and a half later, when Renata's own threat-intel automation finally flags the sign-in IP as malicious.
She pulls the raw sign-in record herself and confirms it: interactive, succeeded, Conditional Access explicitly not applied -- nothing like this account's normal nightly traffic.
Reconstructing the Impossible Travel rule by hand proves the root cause: it excludes this account by an identity tag, entirely, before it ever asks whether the sign-in was interactive at all.
Next: confirming the damage was contained, and shipping the fix.
